fields.meta_title: Animated Landing Page Builder and Examples | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an animated landing page with scroll reveals and demo loops that stay fast and go still for visitors who turn motion off.
fields.h1: Build an Animated Landing Page Where Every Motion Has a Job
fields.hero_description: Build an animated landing page with scroll reveals, counters fed by your database, and a still version for reduced motion.
fields.features_heading: Motion That Earns Its Place on the Page
fields.features_subheading: An animated landing page uses motion to show how a product works or what a total means. Six parts keep it quick and optional.
fields.feature_1:
Describe the motion, get the page

Tell Emergent which parts of the page move, and how long each one runs. It builds the page with those animations in place, and you change any of them later by prompting again.
fields.feature_2:
Reveals that run once, on scroll

Ask for each section to slide up and fade in as it enters the screen. The reveal runs once per visit, so a reader who scrolls back up finds every section already in place.
fields.feature_3:
Counters that read your own numbers

A counter can climb to a total kept in a database you own, such as meals served or orders shipped. Change the number in that row, and the next visitor sees the new total climb.
fields.feature_4:
Motion kept to transform and opacity

Ask Emergent to move, scale, and fade elements, never resize them. web.dev advises you to restrict animations to opacity and transform to keep them on the compositing stage.
fields.feature_5:
A pause button on anything that loops

WCAG 2.2.2 covers motion that starts on its own and lasts more than 5 seconds: visitors need a way to pause, stop, or hide it. Put a pause button on every loop the page plays.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain now, your code later

Publish the page on your own domain; custom domains are included and use credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository, with every animation in it.

fields.tab_content_1:
Step 3 and its form drew 38 of 61 trials

Ferrowick sells invoicing software to plumbing contractors. Its page shows how a finished job becomes an invoice in 3 steps, and each step slides up and fades in as the visitor scrolls down to it. The trial form sits under step 3. Of the 61 trials started this week, 38 came from that form and the rest from the header button.
fields.tab_content_2:
18,400 meals, counted up when the counter scrolls into view

Hollins Street Pantry tops its donation page with one number: meals served this year. Once on screen, the counter climbs from zero to 18,400 meals in 2 seconds. The page reads that total from the pantry's own database on every page load, so last week's deliveries are already counted.
fields.tab_content_3:
An 8-second loop with its own pause button

Quaywise sells shift scheduling to cafes. Its page opens on an 8-second loop of a week's rota filling in, one shift at a time. The loop stops after 3 plays, and a pause button sits in its corner from the first frame. Pellwyn Cafe booked a demo from the form under it.
fields.tab_content_4:
Visitors who ask for less motion see a still hero

Fenwold Design Week runs for 3 days, and its page opens on a drifting hero above a carousel of 24 speakers. A visitor whose device is set to reduce motion gets a still hero and a fixed grid of the same 24 speakers. Both versions show the same registration form, and every registration saves to the event's database.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Animated Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to an animated landing page where each motion has a job, a still version exists, and every form is measured.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what each animation is for
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Set a length for every animation
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Plan a still version of the page
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write one line per animation: what it shows and why it moves. A reveal that walks a visitor through 3 steps has a job; a logo that spins on load does not. Cut any motion you cannot give a job to before you build.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Let the headline, the offer, and the main button load in place with no motion. Save movement for what sits below the first screen, such as steps or a counter. The visitor should read the offer before anything starts to move.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Keep a reveal under half a second so it never holds up reading. Decide how many times a loop plays before it stops, such as 3 plays, instead of leaving it running while the visitor tries to read the text beside it.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask for a version with no drifting hero and no carousel. The prefers-reduced-motion media query detects whether a visitor has asked their device for less motion. With it, the page shows the still version without a toggle.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Describe the page in a prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste the animation list into one prompt with the trigger and length of each, such as a counter that climbs over 2 seconds once it is on screen. Emergent builds the page and its signup table. Prompt again to change the timing of any animation.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Turn on reduced motion and reload
fields.howto_step_6_des: Switch on the reduce motion setting on your phone and load the page again. Check that the hero sits still, the carousel is a fixed grid, and every form still sends. Then load it on a slow connection and watch for text that jumps.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish on your own domain (built into Emergent, uses credits) and count signups by where they started, such as the form under step 3 against the header button. Change one animation at a time, and give each change a full week before you judge it.

faq_plan.q: What is an animated landing page?
faq_plan.a: An animated landing page is a single page with one goal, such as a signup or a demo request, that uses motion to make a point. Steps slide in on scroll, a counter climbs, or a short product loop plays. The offer still reads clearly with every animation switched off.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an animated landing page?
faq_plan.a: List each animation with its job and its length, and keep the headline and main button still. Then describe the page to Emergent's AI landing page builder, which builds it from that prompt, motion included. Before you publish, load it with reduced motion turned on and send a test through every form.

faq_plan.q: Does landing page animation slow down the page?
faq_plan.a: It can, depending on what you animate. web.dev notes that an animation that moves an element using something other than transform is likely to be slow. Slide elements with transform, fade them with opacity, and compress any video loop before it goes on the page.

faq_plan.q: What should I look for in animated landing page examples?
faq_plan.a: Look at when each animation starts and stops, not only how it looks. Scroll each example slowly, then fast, and check that the text reads at both speeds. Then reload it with the reduce motion setting on. If a product needs a minute of motion to explain, study a video landing page instead of a long loop.

faq_plan.q: Should animated landing pages play their animations automatically?
faq_plan.a: Short ones can; long ones need a control. Under WCAG 2.2.2, motion that starts automatically, lasts more than 5 seconds, and plays in parallel with other content needs a pause, stop, or hide control. A counter that finishes in 2 seconds needs nothing extra. A product loop that keeps going needs a pause button.

faq_plan.q: Which landing page animation examples are worth copying?
faq_plan.a: Copy the ones that explain something. A scroll reveal suits a process in 3 steps, a counter suits a running total, and a short loop suits a product doing its main task. Skip motion that only decorates, such as a spinning logo or a headline that types itself out letter by letter.

faq_plan.q: Does a landing page with animation work the same on a phone?
faq_plan.hint: How to make animated landing pages?
faq_plan.a: Not entirely. A phone has no hover, and an effect that plays when a cursor rests on a card never plays there; trigger it on scroll or tap instead. Test on a real phone as well: a mobile landing page is read one screen at a time, and every animation competes for that small space.

faq_plan.q: What code makes landing page animations start on scroll?
faq_plan.a: The Intersection Observer API lets the page observe when an element starts to intersect the viewport, the part of the page on screen. At that moment the page adds a class, and the element slides or fades in. Emergent writes that code from your prompt, and paid plans export it to your GitHub repository.

faq_plan.q: How many animations should an animated landing page have?
faq_plan.a: As few as have a job: at most one per section, and none on the headline or the main button. If two things move on the same screen at once, cut one. Count them before you publish; on a long page, four is plenty.

faq_plan.q: Can an animated landing page include a signup form with steps?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A multi step form fits an animated landing page well: each step slides in after the last answer, and a progress bar fills as the visitor goes. Emergent builds conversational flows with one question per screen, and every answer saves to a database you own.

plan.angle: The SERP for animated landing page is image packs, video carousels and inspiration galleries: they show motion but never say what each animation is for, how long it should run, or what visitors who turn motion off should see. This page shows four animated landing pages where each animation has one job (steps that reveal on scroll, a counter that reads a live total, a demo loop with a pause button, a still version for reduced motion) and gives the rules that keep motion fast and readable: animate transform and opacity, give anything over five seconds a pause control, respect the reduced motion setting. Video, mobile, interactive and modern landing pages are siblings and stay out of the headings.
